name: Enoki
summary: Needs cold fruiting and little fresh air for supermarket-long stems.
chamber_notes: A Shrooly cannot reach true 4 to 10 °C enoki rooms. This profile uses the coolest firmware target (15 °C) and very little fresh air as a chamber approximation.

source_notes.title: Stamets
source_notes.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms (commonly cited chamber ranges). Commercial enoki: ~10 to 16 °C, high CO2, low light, 90 to 95% humidity.

source_notes.title: Vendor cards
source_notes.detail: Home growers who lack a cold room get shorter, darker, more petaled fruits: still edible.

stages.name: Pinning
stages.notes: Keep still and wet to pile up pins.

stages.name: Fruiting
stages.notes: Little fresh air stretches stems. More air makes stocky wild-type caps.

light_recipe.why: Commercial long-stem enoki is grown with little light. Sakamoto 2004 showed a cold dark room makes long pale pinhead fruits; light then forms a cap. This recipe keeps both phases at 0 h so stems stay long. That is a morphology choice from the paper, not a lux number.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 blue is roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum.

sources.title: Sakamoto 2004 enoki
sources.detail: Yuichi Sakamoto, Influence of light on the morphological changes that take place during the development of the Flammulina velutipes fruit body, Mycoscience 45 (2004). A temperature drop induces fruiting in the dark. Dark fruits are long, pale, and pinhead. Light then forms a cap.

sources.title: Sakamoto 2018
sources.detail: Yuichi Sakamoto, Influences of environmental factors on fruiting body induction, development and maturation in mushroom-forming fungi, Fungal Biology Reviews 32 (2018). Light is a fruiting cue for many basidiomycetes. Blue light is the usual photomorphogenesis signal. Agaricus bisporus is called out as not needing light for a cap. Flammulina velutipes can fruit in the dark as a long stem with a tiny cap.

sources.title: Stamets
sources.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms, Ten Speed Press. Used here as a general cultivation reference. This recipe does not take a photoperiod or lux number from a cited page in that book.
